data.content_ref: inline:The proposal explicitly acknowledges that reinstatement as a derived property is broken: the criticism notes lexicographic stratification 'introduces a non-obvious sensitivity to stratum ordering that the flat semantics never had.' Under the original flat skeptical fixed-point semantics, reinstatement of a node follows from the graph structure alone. Once a higher stratum can contain meta-conjectures like 'node y is OUT,' the lexicographic order can let a meta-conjecture in stratum k+1 suppress (or fail to reinstate) a node that stratum k would have reinstated, so reinstatement is no longer a derived property of the argument graph but an artifact of the chosen stratum ordering. That is a direct violation of the problem's requirement to preserve 'reinstatement as a derived property,' and it is independent of the other acknowledged concerns (self-reference expressiveness, polynomial cost).
